newsitem.title: USA: Browning sees $447 mln pre-tax Q4 charge.
newsitem.headline: Browning sees $447 mln pre-tax Q4 charge.

text.p: Browning-Ferris Industries Inc said on Thursday it would take a special pre-tax charge of $447 million in the fourth quarter 1996, for the sale of its Italian operations, divestments and asset write-downs.
The international waste services company also said it planned to cut capital spending in fiscal 1997 to about $790 million from an estimated $1.2 billion in fiscal 1996.
Fourth quarter earnings, due on October 24, would be about $0.33 per share, excluding the $1.80 per share after tax charge for the divestments and write-downs, the company said.
The First Call mean earnings estimate for the quarter was $0.34 per share.

Management decided to sell the Italian operations, divest certain domestic and international non-core business assets and operations and close some recycling facilities which were not expected to reach performance targets, Browning said.
Browning said special charges also included a writedown to fair value of its investment in the Azusa, California landfill.

"This writedown is the result of the changing competitive nature of waste disposal in the Los Angeles market area and the continuing negative legal climate, including recent adverse decisions by the California judicial and regulatory authorities, bearing on the site's ability to accept municipal solid waste," the company said.
The company was not immediately available to comment further on the situation.
The company also said in reducing its capital spending in 1997, it would spend an estimated $690 million in North America and $100 million in international markets.
Browning's revised financial goals included maintaining a strong credit rating and increasing profits at a faster pace than revenues, it said.
The company changed its annual and long-term compensation plans to meet these goals, it said.
